T-0284 (code: `clang_build.build` refuses, on POSIX and before the start, an empty `env` key or one with `=` anywhere, `ValueError` with `parameter` "env"; closes part of ADR-0094 decision 3) stopped on its own criterion 5: its premise does not hold on every supported Python. The task assumed each such key is refused by one of the two POSIX start paths of `subprocess`, so `build` would only refuse earlier what the start refuses anyway. CI (run 39079246945) shows that on Python 3.11 the empty key (`{"": "x"}`, `{b"": b"x"}`) is accepted by both start calls (3.11 uses fork/exec with the default `close_fds=True`; the `posix_spawn` path that refuses it is taken by default only from 3.13), while the leading-`=` keys are refused as assumed; on 3.14 all cases hold. `pyproject.toml` requires Python >= 3.11. The change is on Draft PR #179 (DONOTMERGE, branch `claude/T-0284-clang-build-refuses-posix-env-keys`, `e1a40c9`, 1 review round, Request changes); nothing was merged. Should the driver (a) keep the empty key in scope, so `build` refuses it on POSIX even where `subprocess` does not (stricter than `subprocess`, with the docstring saying so), and re-run T-0284 on that basis; (b) narrow T-0284 to keys with `=` (which held on 3.11 and 3.14) and leave the empty key to `subprocess`; or (c) drop T-0284 and close PR #179?

T-0286 (code: `local_run.run` refuses, before the start, an `env` that is not `None` and has no `items` method with a `TypeError` carrying `parameter` "env", as T-0282 did for `clang_build.build`) stopped on its own criterion 3: some `subprocess` start path accepts such an `env`. On native Windows (Python 3.14.4, seen on the driver machine) `subprocess.run` with an `env` object that has only `keys`, `values`, `__getitem__` and `__len__` starts the child and passes the variables on; `local_run.run` takes that path on Windows (no `os.wait4`). By the CPython source the POSIX `posix_spawn` path, which `run` meets the conditions for, also reads `env` through `keys`/`values`; only fork/exec calls `env.items()`. Refusing every such `env` would make the docstring sentence 'The check refuses nothing that one of the ways subprocess starts a process accepts' false. Nothing was committed and no PR was opened. Should `local_run.run` (a) refuse every non-`None` `env` without `items` with `TypeError` (`parameter` "env") as `clang_build.build` does, dropping that sentence for this case; (b) refuse only an `env` that no start path accepts (for example one with neither `items` nor `keys`/`values`/`__getitem__`), keeping the sentence true; or (c) stay unchanged? And should `clang_build.build` (T-0282, 4e05627, already stricter than Windows `subprocess`) be aligned with the answer?
